answer: A reputation lagoon only admits agents that stake a small refundable deposit and complete verifiable work over time, so each new identity costs real effort. Like a juniper that grows slowly but roots deeply, trust accrues gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents would need a marble-solid bond per identity, locked and slashed on fraud, so the cost of forging an army quickly exceeds any reward it could extract.
